findings.claim: The token refusal told the user to give the token to "the step that posts the report", but under this change a separate publish job posts it.

verdict.text: This was a narrow round on f1, and f1 is fixed.
The refusal in `action/agent.py` and the copy quoted in the how-to now say the same thing and match the two-job design.
The stamp is green, so the fix broke nothing.

`action/agent.py:480-481`: the refusal now reads "refused: {name} is set, and the agent could read the token. Give it only to the publish job, which runs no agent." `docs/how-to/install-the-plugin-and-the-ci-action.md:342`: quotes the same text with the `agent: ` prefix, and lines 345-348 around it describe the publish job the same way.
I grepped the tree for the old phrase "posts the report".
The only hits are history: an `.okf/log.md` entry and a past-tense passage in ADR 0017.
Neither repeats the old refusal, and no test pins the old text.
I ran `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree myself.
All passed: lint, format, tests, integration, and eval rows r1 through r7.
The refusal at `action/agent.py:481` and its quote at `docs/how-to/install-the-plugin-and-the-ci-action.md:342` now both say "Give it only to the publish job, which runs no agent."
